title: Reframe a Negative
html: tive light. It's a "yes, and" approach rather than a "yes, but." This seems to do a few things at once. It makes the other person feel heard, since their point isn't being dismissed outright. It avoids the defensiveness that often comes from immediate pushback. And it shifts the conversation from "what's wrong" to "what we can do," which keeps momentum and optimism intact even when discussing something negative. I want to start practicing this more deliberately, especially in moments where my instinct is to jump straight to a counterpoint or solution.
